symptoms: runny nose, sneezing, mild sore throat, mild cough, congestion
advice: Rest, stay hydrated, use steam inhalation, warm salt water gargle for sore throat.
see_doctor_if: symptoms last beyond 10 days or fever exceeds 102F

symptoms: fever, body ache, chills, fatigue, dry cough, headache
advice: Rest, fluids, monitor temperature. Isolate to avoid spreading.
see_doctor_if: fever persists beyond 3 days or breathing becomes difficult

symptoms: throbbing one-sided headache, nausea, light sensitivity, sound sensitivity
advice: Rest in a dark quiet room, stay hydrated, avoid triggers like screens.
see_doctor_if: headache is sudden and the worst you have ever had, or comes with confusion

symptoms: dull pressure headache, tight band around head, neck stiffness
advice: Rest, hydration, gentle neck stretches, reduce screen time.
see_doctor_if: headache is persistent daily for over 2 weeks

symptoms: burning chest sensation after eating, sour taste, bloating
advice: Avoid spicy/oily food, eat smaller meals, avoid lying down right after eating.
see_doctor_if: symptoms occur more than twice a week or you have trouble swallowing

symptoms: upper stomach pain, bloating, nausea after eating, mild burning
advice: Avoid spicy and acidic food, eat smaller frequent meals.
see_doctor_if: pain is severe or there is vomiting with blood

symptoms: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach cramps, started after eating
advice: Stay hydrated with oral rehydration solution, rest, eat bland food (rice, banana).
see_doctor_if: symptoms last more than 2 days or there is blood in stool

symptoms: watery diarrhea, vomiting, mild fever, stomach cramps
advice: Hydration is key, small frequent sips of ORS, avoid dairy and oily food.
see_doctor_if: signs of dehydration like dizziness or very reduced urination

symptoms: burning urination, frequent urge to urinate, cloudy urine, lower abdominal discomfort
advice: Drink plenty of water, avoid holding urine. Needs medical evaluation for antibiotics.
see_doctor_if: fever, back pain, or blood in urine appears

symptoms: sneezing, itchy eyes, runny nose, nasal congestion, triggered by dust/pollen
advice: Avoid known triggers, keep windows closed during high pollen, wash face after outdoor exposure.
see_doctor_if: symptoms interfere significantly with sleep or daily activity

symptoms: red itchy patch of skin, mild swelling, appeared after contact with new product
advice: Avoid the irritant, keep area clean and dry, avoid scratching.
see_doctor_if: rash spreads rapidly or is accompanied by fever

symptoms: localized redness, itching, mild swelling at bite site
advice: Clean the area, cold compress, avoid scratching.
see_doctor_if: swelling spreads beyond the bite area or breathing difficulty occurs

symptoms: small skin break, minor bleeding, mild pain
advice: Clean with water, apply antiseptic, cover with a clean bandage.
see_doctor_if: wound is deep, won't stop bleeding, or shows signs of infection (pus, spreading redness)

symptoms: localized muscle pain after activity, stiffness, mild swelling
advice: Rest the area, ice for first 24-48 hours, gentle stretching after.
see_doctor_if: severe pain, inability to move the area, or visible deformity

symptoms: racing thoughts, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, mild chest tightness without cardiac history
advice: Practice slow breathing, reduce caffeine, talk to someone you trust.
medicine_category: none - lifestyle and professional support recommended
see_doctor_if: symptoms are persistent, affecting daily life, or include thoughts of self-harm

symptoms: difficulty falling asleep, waking frequently at night, daytime fatigue
advice: Keep a consistent sleep schedule, avoid screens before bed, limit caffeine after noon.
see_doctor_if: insomnia persists beyond 3 weeks

symptoms: red eyes, itching, watery or sticky discharge, no vision change
advice: Avoid touching/rubbing eyes, wash hands frequently, use clean cloth for discharge.
see_doctor_if: vision changes, significant eye pain, or sensitivity to light

symptoms: thirst, dry mouth, fatigue, reduced urination, mild dizziness on standing
advice: Increase fluid intake, add electrolytes if sweating heavily.
see_doctor_if: confusion, fainting, or no urination for 8+ hours

symptoms: infrequent bowel movements, straining, hard stool, bloating
advice: Increase fiber and water intake, light physical activity.
see_doctor_if: severe abdominal pain, blood in stool, or no relief after a few days

symptoms: dry or mild productive cough persisting after a cold, no fever
advice: Warm fluids, honey and warm water, humidify the air.
see_doctor_if: cough lasts more than 3 weeks or is accompanied by blood

symptoms: body temperature 99-101F, mild fatigue, no other alarming symptoms
advice: Rest, fluids, monitor temperature every few hours.
see_doctor_if: fever exceeds 103F or lasts more than 3 days

symptoms: facial pressure, nasal congestion, thick nasal discharge, mild headache
advice: Steam inhalation, saline nasal rinse, stay hydrated.
see_doctor_if: symptoms persist beyond 10 days or severe facial pain develops

symptoms: pain when swallowing, scratchy throat, mild fever possible
advice: Warm salt water gargle, warm fluids, throat lozenges.
see_doctor_if: severe difficulty swallowing, drooling, or high fever

symptoms: nausea, dizziness during travel, cold sweat
advice: Look at a fixed distant point, fresh air, avoid reading while moving.
see_doctor_if: symptoms persist long after travel ends

symptoms: red, warm, tender skin after sun exposure, no blistering
advice: Cool compress, moisturizer, stay hydrated, avoid further sun exposure.
see_doctor_if: blistering, fever, or widespread severe burn

symptoms: flaky scalp, mild itching, no redness or pain
advice: Use gentle anti-dandruff shampoo, avoid excessive hot water on scalp.
see_doctor_if: scalp becomes red, painful, or shows signs of infection

symptoms: lower abdominal cramping during period, mild back pain
advice: Warm compress, light exercise, rest as needed.
see_doctor_if: pain is severe, unusual, or accompanied by heavy bleeding

symptoms: heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness, nausea after heat exposure
advice: Move to a cool place immediately, hydrate, remove excess clothing.
see_doctor_if: confusion, very high body temperature, or stops sweating (possible heat stroke - emergency)

symptoms: muffled hearing, mild ear discomfort, no pain or discharge
advice: Avoid inserting objects into ear, consider ear drops to soften wax.
see_doctor_if: ear pain, discharge, or sudden hearing loss develops

symptoms: fullness, mild discomfort after a large meal, occasional burping
advice: Eat slowly, avoid overeating, avoid lying down immediately after meals.
see_doctor_if: pain radiates to chest/arm or is accompanied by sweating (seek emergency care)
